About The Role

Adobe is seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join the Adobe Genuine Engineering team. This group protects Adobe's ecosystem from fraud, abuse, and misuse using intelligent systems worldwide.

In this position, you will build and develop machine learning models from scratch, including custom transformer-based frameworks, to identify fraudulent actions, stop account sharing, and protect the experience of hundreds of millions of users. You will manage the entire model lifecycle: raw behavioral data and feature engineering, architecture development, large-scale GPU training, deployment, and monitoring.

The team is actively building in-house behavioral foundation models that learn identity-preserving representations from long sequences of user activity. This is a role for an engineer who wants to own deep learning systems end-to-end — not consume pre-built ones.

Key Responsibilities

• Build and train deep learning models from scratch, including custom transformer and attention-based architectures for long behavioral event sequences. 
• Own the full training stack: event tokenization, temporal and positional embeddings, self-supervised pretraining (e.g., masked modeling, contrastive learning), and downstream fine-tuning. 
• Train large models efficiently on GPU infrastructure using mixed-precision training, gradient accumulation/checkpointing, efficient attention, and distributed strategies (DDP, FSDP, or equivalent). 
• Build and optimize feature pipelines on Databricks and Spark, transforming raw behavioral events into high-quality model inputs. 
• Translate prototypes into production ML systems — scalable, reliable, and observable — and drive inference performance through architectural and serving-side optimization. 
• Contribute to MLOps practices: experiment tracking, model versioning, CI/CD, automated retraining, and production monitoring. 
• Collaborate cross-functionally with data science, product, and platform teams; mentor junior engineers on experimentation rigor, deployment process, and responsible AI. 
• Stay current with advances in ML/AI and bring relevant innovations into Adobe's products. 

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, or related field. 
• 5+ years of professional experience building and deploying ML solutions at scale. 
• Strong programming expertise in Python, with hands-on experience in PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar frameworks. 
• Deep understanding of the end-to-end ML lifecycle—from data collection to deployment and monitoring. 
• Strong grasp of model optimization, inference efficiency, and production system integration. 

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in fraud detection, anomaly detection, or behavioral modeling.

You'll join a small but high-impact Accounting & Controlling team at a pivotal moment in Typeform's journey.

As we've grown into a global SaaS business, our finance function is evolving to support greater scale, complexity, and ambition. We're investing in stronger financial controls, more sophisticated accounting operations, and systems that will enable our next stage of growth.

You'll partner closely with the VP of Accounting & Controlling, serving as their strategic deputy and helping lead both the day-to-day function and the longer-term evolution of our accounting organization. Together, you'll build a world-class finance operation that is scalable, resilient, and ready for what's next.

As Director of Accounting & Controlling, you'll lead the operational accounting function while helping shape the future of finance at Typeform.

Reporting to the VP of Accounting & Controlling, you'll own the integrity of our global accounting operations, oversee a growing team, and drive initiatives that strengthen financial controls, improve efficiency, and support international growth. You'll combine technical accounting expertise with strong leadership and operational excellence, ensuring the business continues to scale on solid financial foundations.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You'll be a trusted partner to senior leadership, mentor and develop the accounting team, and play a key role in transforming how finance operates across the company.

Things you will do:

• Lead the Accounting & Controlling function, ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant financial operations across multiple entities and jurisdictions

• Partner closely with the VP of Accounting & Controlling as a strategic deputy, helping define priorities, lead the team, and drive the finance roadmap

• Manage, coach, and develop a high-performing accounting team, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence

• Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close processes, ensuring high-quality financial reporting and strong balance sheet integrity

• Strengthen our internal control environment and ensure compliance with IFRS and regulatory requirements across all operating jurisdictions

• Oversee revenue recognition policies and processes across our subscription and usage-based business models

• Lead our indirect tax strategy and compliance (VAT/GST, digital services taxes, and related obligations), partnering with external advisors where appropriate

• Oversee transfer pricing frameworks, intercompany accounting, and cross-border financial operations

• Partner with Legal, FP&A, People, and external advisors to support international expansion, entity creation, and regulatory compliance

• Lead external audits and statutory reporting processes, ensuring smooth execution and strong stakeholder relationships

• Drive finance transformation initiatives, including process redesign, automation, ERP optimization, and scalability improvements

• Build internal accounting capabilities while reducing dependency on external advisors where appropriate

• Provide leadership and continuity for the function, acting on behalf of the VP of Accounting & Controlling when required

What you already bring to the table:

• Significant experience leading accounting and controlling functions within a high-growth technology or SaaS environment

• Experience managing and developing accounting teams in a fast-paced, international business

• Strong technical accounting expertise with deep knowledge of IFRS

• Proven experience managing multi-entity, multi-jurisdiction accounting environments

• Strong understanding of revenue recognition, particularly for subscription and usage-based business models

• Experience overseeing indirect tax compliance across multiple jurisdictions

• Strong understanding of financial controls, risk management, and audit processes

• Experience partnering with executive stakeholders and influencing cross-functional decisions

• A pragmatic, hands-on leadership style with a willingness to dive into the details when needed

• Excellent communication skills and the ability to build trusted relationships across the business

• A continuous improvement mindset with experience driving operational excellence and finance transformation

• Experience with international expansion, entity setup, and cross-border compliance

• Strong knowledge of transfer pricing and international tax structures

• Big 4 background or equivalent public accounting experience

Role Overview
Neon is a gaming-focused Merchant of Record platform serving game publishers globally. We process payments across 50+ markets through multiple PSPs simultaneously, operating as the seller of record across card networks, local wallets, A2A rails, and alternative payment methods.

This role owns the operational backbone of that system: dispute and chargeback management, fraud operations, compliance monitoring, payment performance tracking, and operational support for Customer Success. As the senior operator across these functions, the Payment Operations Manager sets operational standards, defines targets, owns PSP and partner operational relationships, and is accountable for outcomes across payments, risk, fraud, and compliance. The role partners with the Head of Payments and the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader as a peer across all four functions.

This is a senior individual-contributor role. The Manager title reflects the seniority and ownership scope of the role and function, not direct reports at this stage.

Scope & Responsibilities
Dispute & Chargeback Operations
• 
Own dispute intake, evidence compilation, and resolution across all active payment processors and markets.
• 
Define and own resolution SLAs and win-rate targets; identify systemic patterns and drive fixes with product and risk leads.
• 
Prioritize and drive the roadmap for internal dispute tooling as operational infrastructure matures.
Fraud Operations
• 
Own fraud operations and oversee investigations and transaction reviews in partnership with the Risk, Fraud & Compliance Product Leader.
• 
Set monitoring and escalation standards across screening and decisioning tools; maintain case integrity and decision quality.
• 
Track fraud loss trends across markets and game titles; surface and act on emerging attack patterns before they scale.
Payment Performance Monitoring
• 
Own tracking of authorization rates, payment success rates, decline codes, and fraud losses across processors and markets.
• 
Own post-launch metric reviews for new payment methods against defined performance thresholds.
• 
Define the operational dashboard and alerting standard; ensure anomalies are caught before they become publisher-impacting incidents.
Customer Success Support
• 
Serve as the senior operational point of contact for payment-related requests escalated by Customer Success.
• 
Lead deep dives into publisher payment performance, dispute trends, and fraud exposure, producing structured analysis CS can use directly in publisher conversations.
• 
Own the operational response to payment incidents: root cause investigation, timeline reconstruction, and remediation communication.
PSP & Partner Management
• 
Own day-to-day operational relationships with PSPs and payment partners, including performance reviews, escalations, and issue resolution.
• 
Hold partners accountable to performance and SLA commitments; drive improvement where markets or methods underperform.
Process, Tooling & Standards
• 
Set and maintain operational standards, runbooks, and process documentation that others follow.
• 
Prioritize automation opportunities and partner with the Head of Payments, Risk & Compliance, and engineering to translate operational gaps into product and tooling improvements.
• 
Act as the senior escalation point for payment operations.

Key Success Metrics
• 
Dispute win rate and resolution turnaround, owned and improved per processor.
• 
Fraud operations outcomes: fraud loss rate, false positive rate, detection rate, and escalation accuracy.
• 
PSR performance against target across active payment methods and markets, with defined review triggers on all methods.
• 
Incident response and resolution time for publisher-impacting payment issues.
• 
Reporting accuracy, on-time delivery, and operational process maturity as the function scales.

Ideal Profile
• 
6-8+ years in payments operations, fraud ops, or fintech risk, with a track record of owning a function or leading operational initiatives, ideally at a PSP, Merchant of Record, or digital goods company.
• 
Has run these functions end to end, not just participated in them; comfortable operating across multiple payment processors simultaneously, with direct experience of global PSPs such as Stripe, Adyen, PayPal, or Razorpay.
• 
Experience owning PSP or partner relationships and influencing product, engineering, and Customer Success without formal authority.
• 
Deep understanding of dispute and chargeback mechanics at the card network level (Visa/Mastercard rules), not just tool navigation.
• 
Strong analytical capability: works across dashboards and data tools, builds structured reports, and finds signals in noisy transaction data.
• 
Detail-oriented and self-directing; operates with significant autonomy across a broad and growing operational surface.
• 
Business-level English proficiency required, written and verbal.
